overview: Automotive engineers develop cars, trucks and their systems, from engines and batteries to brakes and power electronics. They design parts, run system-level tests, find root causes of failures and guide other engineers and technicians. O*NET rates knowledge of engineering and technology at 4.71 out of 5 for this job and physics at 4.35. Most hold a bachelor's degree in mechanical or a related engineering field, 71% in O*NET data. BLS reports pay only for the broader mechanical engineers group, with a median of $104,110. Michigan is the center of the industry.
pay: BLS reports pay for the wider mechanical engineers group, which includes automotive engineers. Its median is $104,110, and the top 10% earn $164,340 or more. Michigan has the most of these jobs, 34,630, at a median of $104,890. New Mexico has the highest state median, $157,710, mostly in federal labs.

faq.q: How much do automotive engineers make?
faq.a: BLS reports pay for the broader mechanical engineers group: a May 2025 median of $104,110. The middle half earn between $84,130 and $132,590. California pays a median of $130,900, while Michigan, the center of the auto industry, pays $104,890. Kansas and Arkansas have the lowest state medians.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be an automotive engineer?
faq.a: Most automotive engineers have a bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical or electromechanical engineering. In O*NET data, 71% hold a bachelor's degree and 14% a master's degree. Electric vehicle and battery roles increasingly value electrical engineering and software skills, and many engineers learn them on the job.

faq.q: What skills do automotive engineers need?
faq.a: O*NET rates critical thinking at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and reading comprehension at 4. Mathematics and writing are rated 3.88. Root cause analysis, testing and clear reporting are central, and intellectual curiosity stands out as a work style.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to automotive engineer?
faq.a: The closest moves are Materials Scientists (81% match), industrial engineering technologists (78%) and Mechanical Drafters (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Materials Scientists earn a median of $117,790, and Remote Sensing Scientists, a 76% match, earn $122,570, according to BLS May 2025.
